fields.description:
## Context

Sibling-emitted candidate fixture specs assert a criterion should fire or stay silent for a real
plan — from history, not current code. Such a candidate is either wrong or evidence of
drift; a wrong must-fire case admitted unverified encodes a false positive as required behavior. One
run cannot settle it — byte-identical material flipped verdict in 208 of 551 store pairs, so shipped
specs use `epochs: 3`/`gate: at_least(2)`.

## Approach

**Rehydrate, then run.** The selector manifest lists candidates per criterion, each carrying
`direction` (fire/no_fire) and a `review_event_uuid` — the join key to the review sidecar
(`fixture_selection.py` schema). A candidate's emitter `input` is a model-free
provenance descriptor, NOT plan text, so the runner does NOT run the finder on it. It loads the
sidecar corpus the selector used (`corpus.build_corpus(store_roots, cache_dir=...)`, persisting
verified rows that carry the at-review material — `description` and `children` — keyed by
`review_event_uuid`; `corpus.py:_build_sidecar_row`), and REHYDRATES each case's finder input from
the row matching the candidate's `review_event_uuid`: `description` as plan text (plus `children` as
the roster for a container criterion). A candidate resolving to no verified row is withheld to drift as
unrecoverable material (no finder call). It then runs the criterion's real current Pass-1 finder via
`eval_solver.run_case(prompt_id, case, runner=live, repo_root=repo_root)` (`eval_solver.py:322`)
with `case["input"]` the rehydrated material — not `calibrate_criterion`, which only scores an
existing dataset (`eval.py:69-78`). Each case runs
three times; `_fired(verdict)` (a finding present) is the observed verdict; a case matching its
`expect` (`finding`/`pass`) in ≥2 of 3 runs REPRODUCES (current code still agrees with history).

**Disposition.** A reproducing case is kept; a non-reproducing one is withheld to a drift report at
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/fixtures/drift-report.md` (criterion, case id, predicted vs
observed behavior, originating review `(ticket_id, review_event_uuid)` from the matched row). To
write a criterion's spec the runner reuses the emitter's strict-only skeleton — `prompt`, `model`,
`epochs`, `gate`, `coverage_threshold`, `scorers` (the deterministic gating scorer) — UNCHANGED, and
rebuilds `dataset` + `gold_set` (1:1 input/label) from only the reproducing cases, each case's
`input` being the runnable rehydrated material. The spec is written to
`.rebar/evals/<prompt-id>.eval.yaml` via a temp file + atomic `os.replace` only when the filtered
dataset is balanced (both sides non-empty) with a non-empty `gold_set` and
`validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` returns zero errors; else the criterion is withheld. The
runner returns an in-memory summary (admitted/withheld ids, drift entries, total spend); the drift
report and admitted specs are the only files written.

**No-shadowing guard.** A user `.rebar/evals/<id>.eval.yaml` WINS over a packaged built-in at load
(`eval_spec_path` before `_packaged_eval_spec`), so the runner SKIPS any criterion whose id is a
packaged built-in in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/`. A same-id `.rebar/evals/` file is a prior
artifact (overwritten by the atomic write), NOT a shadow — never skipped.

**Budget enforcement.** Before each criterion the run pre-flights
`ledger.reserve(estimate_usd, ledger_path=<epic ledger>, cap_usd=250.0, reserve_usd=0.0)` against
this epic's `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/fixtures/ledger.jsonl` (reserve_usd=0 ⇒ ceiling
exactly $250), then `finalize()`s priced ACTUAL usage. Because `finalize` prices real tokens that
can exceed the estimate, after EACH `finalize` the run re-reads cumulative actual spend and, if it
now meets/exceeds `cap_usd`, halts FATALLY before any further criterion — so $250 bounds actual
finalized spend. The estimate tier follows the criterion's `exec` routing
(`criteria.effective_routing`, ADR 0033); `exec: DET` is out of scope. Model parity pinned to
production Pass-1 per ADR 0109.

**Failure disposition.** Per criterion the two writes are STRICTLY ORDERED — atomic spec
`os.replace` FIRST, ledger `finalize()` SECOND — with the ledger the sole resume oracle: a criterion
is done iff its stable `run_id = f"admission-{prompt_id}"` is in the ledger. Crash between the two ⇒
no ledger row ⇒ resume re-derives and the atomic write overwrites the orphan spec (one row, one
charge); crash after `finalize` ⇒ the spec already exists. A transient model/transport error is
RETRYABLE (3 attempts, exp backoff 1s/2s/4s), then the criterion is left incomplete (no ledger row; run
continues). Both a `reserve` `BudgetExceeded` and the post-`finalize` cap breach are
FATAL, stopping with finalized criteria admitted; `reconcile` recharges no recorded `run_id`.

## Scope

The admission runner, its rehydration + disposition logic, the drift-report writer, and the
`.rebar/evals/` specs.

## Non-goals

Repairing drift (each entry becomes a ticket linked `discovered_from` the epic); editing
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`; scheduling re-runs (the sibling self-healing loop owns it).

## Testing

Unit tests drive disposition with a scripted stub solver and stub sidecar index (no model); the live
run covers the real path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A must-fire case whose `review_event_uuid` resolves to a sidecar row runs the finder on that
      row's rehydrated `description` (not the descriptor); scripted (fire, fire, silent) it is
      admitted into the criterion's dataset with that runnable material as its `input` (`pytest`).
- [ ] A must-fire case scripted (fire, silent, silent) is withheld with a drift entry
      (criterion, case id, predicted/observed, review `(ticket_id, review_event_uuid)`); a case whose
      `review_event_uuid` matches no verified row is likewise withheld as unrecoverable material,
      no finder call (`pytest`).
- [ ] With the ledger at the ceiling, the first `reserve` raises `BudgetExceeded` and a
      call-counting stub reports `0` model calls (`pytest`).
- [ ] When a finalized criterion's ACTUAL spend reaches/passes `cap_usd`, the run halts before the
      next criterion (the breaching one stays admitted); `pytest` prices synthetic rows above the
      estimate.
- [ ] Every written spec passes `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)`, the real validator run over
      each file (`pytest`).
- [ ] A criterion matching a packaged built-in in `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` is skipped while a
      same-id `.rebar/evals/` prior artifact is NOT; `pytest` asserts written and packaged basenames
      are disjoint and the pre-seeded id was processed.
- [ ] A criterion writes no `.eval.yaml` when its reproducing cases leave one side empty (drifting
      its cases) or when a case raises before all finish (no partial file) (`pytest`).
- [ ] Resume is crash-consistent (`pytest`): a re-run recharges no finalized criterion (`reconcile`
      returns the existing row, zero new calls); a spec file with no ledger row (crash between
      writes) is re-derived to one ledger row.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live admission run has completed over the full candidate set with the Pass-1
      model pinned to its production class, and this epic's ledger records total spend >0 and ≤250.0
      with a per-pass model id on every row.
      provenance: environment=developer workstation against the production Bedrock chain;
      principal=the Bedrock plan-review identity; privilege_posture=production-equivalent;
      instrument=live-call.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Each drift-report entry has a ticket linked `discovered_from` the parent epic.
      provenance: environment=the rebar tickets store; principal=the session's rebar assignee;
      privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`/`make typecheck`/`make test` pass; live run completed; drift report and admitted specs
committed; cumulative ledger spend ≤ $250.
